name: PandaX
full_name: Particle and Astrophysical Xenon Experiments - neutrino programme
summary: PandaX is a xenon-detector programme at Jinping studying dark matter, solar neutrinos and rare decays. Its liquid-xenon PandaX-4T stage completed operation in April 2026 and the collaboration is constructing PandaX-20T. PandaX-III is a separate gaseous-xenon double-beta project.
detection_principle: The dual-phase xenon TPC measures prompt light and delayed charge-induced electroluminescence. Position reconstruction and the charge-to-light ratio separate backgrounds and interaction types.

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: PandaX-4T stopped operation on 17 April 2026 after Run 11162. The collaboration is constructing PandaX-20T; deployment in late 2026 and construction completion in 2027 are plans, not completed milestones.

timeline.event: PandaX-4T completed its final data-taking run.

collaboration.name: PandaX Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: PandaX-4T target
key_parameters.value: Approximately 4 tonnes of active liquid xenon

key_parameters.name: Neutrino signals
key_parameters.value: Solar electron recoils, coherent nuclear recoils and xenon rare decays

phases.name: PandaX-I / PandaX-II
phases.description: Earlier liquid-xenon dark-matter and rare-event stages.

phases.name: PandaX-4T
phases.description: Stopped operation on 17 April 2026; analyses of accumulated data continue.

phases.name: PandaX-20T
phases.description: Construction underway; late-2026 deployment and 2027 completion were forecast in September 2026.

results.summary: The PandaX programme has published neutrino and rare-decay analyses; the future PandaX-xT scale is documented separately.
The collaboration reported a solar pp-neutrino flux measurement from its 2024-2026 Run 2 electron-recoil data; publication after shutdown does not mean the detector is still taking data.

science_scope: Neutrino interaction measurements and double-beta-decay searches are part of a multipurpose dark-matter detector programme. Different analyses use different event selections, fiducial masses and exposure periods.
